USMLE-style practice · Pathology

Granuloma with central debris

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient has weight loss, chronic cough, and an upper-lobe cavitary lesion. Biopsy shows epithelioid macrophages surrounding a central granular acellular area; acid-fast organisms are identified. Which necrosis pattern is most consistent with these findings?

  1. Caseous necrosis
  2. Coagulative necrosis
  3. Enzymatic fat necrosis
  4. Fibrinoid necrosis
  5. Isolated apoptotic-body formation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Caseous necrosis

Tuberculous granulomas commonly contain central caseous material.

Understanding the options

Caseous necrosis
Tuberculous granulomas commonly contain central caseous material.
Coagulative necrosis
Recognizable tissue outlines are not the defining feature of caseation.
Enzymatic fat necrosis
This centers on adipose tissue and calcium soaps.
Fibrinoid necrosis
This is a vessel-wall pattern rather than the granuloma center.
Isolated apoptotic-body formation
Apoptosis involves individual-cell fragments rather than a large caseous center.
